marks.gloss_en: וכי תימא: what difference does it make to us?
וכי תימא: we check it [after it falls]
the mishna (Yoma): it had not reached halfway down the mountain before it was torn limb from limb
the striker of his father is executed, yet we do not fear he is not his father -- most intercourse is the husband's
Rav Mari: from one who strikes his father or mother, whom the Torah executes -- let us fear he is not his father! rather, we follow the majority: most intercourse is the husband's
ממאי? perhaps his father and mother were imprisoned together
the murderer is executed, yet we do not fear the victim was a tereifa
Rav Kahana: from the murderer, whom the Torah executes -- let us fear the victim was a tereifa! rather, we follow the majority
וכי תימא: we check the victim
וכי תימא: for the murderer's life, let us mutilate (aimed at ref_ka_minaval)
conspiring witnesses are executed, yet we do not fear the accused was a tereifa
Ravina: from conspiring witnesses (Deut 19:19) -- let us fear the man they testified against was a tereifa! rather, we follow the majority
וכי תימא: we check him
Beribbi: if they have not yet killed, they are killed; if they killed, they are not killed
'slaughter and eat', yet we do not fear he cut at a hole
Rav Ashi: from slaughter itself -- 'slaughter and eat'; let us fear he cut at the place of a hole! rather, we follow the majority
ודלמא היכא דאפשר אפשר, היכא דלא אפשר לא אפשר (= p_heikha_deefshar; in the ואמרי לה version said by Rav Shimi)
perhaps where it is possible [to check] it is required; where it is not possible, not -- the majority is relied on only where checking is impossible
דאי לא תימא הכי: R' Meir, concerned for the minority, would eat no meat
וכי תימא הכי נמי -- indeed he would not
R' Meir is concerned for the minority
